_what: One row per inbound channel. This is the connection register: what the mechanism is, what we control, what the provider controls, what is still missing, and who has to do something about it. Nothing here activates anything. A channel becomes live by configuring credentials and a webhook at the provider, verifying, and switching mode from test to live - not by changing code.

_readiness.not_prepared: No adapter exists on our side.
_readiness.ready_for_configuration: Our side is finished. It needs credentials and a provider setting, nothing more.
_readiness.waiting_for_external_access: Our side is finished but somebody outside this repository must grant access, approve an app, or answer a question first.
_readiness.manual_only: The provider offers no inbound mechanism we can rely on. A person enters it by hand, and that is the design, not a gap.
_readiness.capability_unconfirmed: We do not know whether the provider can do this. EXTERNAL CONFIRMATION REQUIRED before anything is promised.

_modes: Every channel has a mode: off, test or live. Only 'test' accepts a simulated payload. 'live' additionally requires real credentials to be present, and nothing in this repository can set it.
_idempotency: Every adapter declares an externalId. The inbound table has a unique index on (channel, external_id), so the same provider event delivered twice is stored once. Providers retry; that is normal and must never make two people.

website.label: Website form
website.mechanism: We publish an endpoint. The website posts to it.
website.rateLimit: Ours to set. A public form needs a spam control in front of it.
providerControls: nothing - this is our own website
website.externalActionRequired: Whoever maintains the website points the form at the endpoint and sets the same secret.
website.howWeTest: Simulate from DEV CONTROL, or post a fixture to the endpoint with the test secret.
website.howWeGoLive: Deploy, set the secret both sides, send one real submission, check it appears in CAR, switch mode to live.
website.howWeDisable: Set the channel mode to off. The endpoint then refuses and says so.

google_form.label: Google Form
google_form.mechanism: Apps Script on the response sheet posts to our endpoint on submit.
google_form.rateLimit: Apps Script quotas apply to the sender, not to us.
google_form.externalBlocker: Somebody who owns the form must paste the script, add the installable trigger and authorise it once.
providerControls: the field names on the form
credentialsNeeded: GOOGLE_FORM_SECRET, generated by us and pasted into the script
google_form.externalActionRequired: The form owner runs the script once and approves the permission prompt.
google_form.howWeTest: Simulate from DEV CONTROL using the documented Apps Script payload.
google_form.howWeGoLive: Deploy, install the script, submit one real test response, check CAR, switch to live.
google_form.howWeDisable: Remove the trigger at Google, or set the mode to off here.
google_form._note: A second architecture exists - the Forms API with a Cloud project and Pub/Sub. It is heavier and needs a Cloud project. The Apps Script route is what this contract assumes. EXTERNAL CONFIRMATION REQUIRED on which one Novikontas wants.

gmail.label: Email
gmail.mechanism: We poll the Gmail API for new messages. Push over Pub/Sub is possible later.
gmail.rateLimit: Gmail API quota per user. Polling every few minutes is well inside it.
gmail.externalBlocker: A Google Cloud project, a service account, and a Workspace ADMIN granting domain-wide delegation for edu@novikontas.org.
gmail.externalActionRequired: The Google Workspace administrator authorises domain-wide delegation. This is not something a normal user can do.
gmail.howWeTest: Simulate from DEV CONTROL with a Gmail-shaped message fixture.
gmail.howWeGoLive: Deploy, add the key, poll once by hand, check CAR, then enable the schedule.
gmail.howWeDisable: Disable the schedule. The key can also be revoked at Google.
gmail.bodyRetention: The message body is held only until somebody qualifies or archives the item, then deleted. What survives is the structured record. Decided 23.09.2026.

facebook.label: Facebook
facebook.mechanism: Meta sends a webhook to us when a message or lead arrives.
facebook.externalIdSource: the message id, or leadgen_id for a lead form
facebook.timestampSource: the event timestamp, seconds since epoch
facebook.rateLimit: Meta rate limits apply to our calls back to them, not to their webhook.
facebook.externalBlocker: A Meta app, page access from the business portfolio, and APP REVIEW for messaging permissions. Review takes weeks and can be refused.
facebook.externalActionRequired: Confirm WHO owns the page and the business portfolio, create the app, subscribe the page, pass App Review.
facebook.howWeTest: Simulate from DEV CONTROL with a Meta-shaped webhook body, signed with a test secret.
facebook.howWeGoLive: Deploy, set the callback URL and verify token at Meta, pass the handshake, send one real message, switch to live.
facebook.howWeDisable: Unsubscribe the page at Meta, or set the mode to off here.
facebook.operationalNote: Facebook and Instagram are worked through the shared Meta Business Suite inbox. The channel is Facebook; who owns the person in the CRM is decided after qualification and is not the same question.

messenger.label: Messenger
messenger.mechanism: Meta webhook. The same connection as Facebook; the originating channel is recorded separately.
messenger.externalIdSource: the message id, or leadgen_id for a lead form
messenger.timestampSource: the event timestamp, seconds since epoch
messenger.rateLimit: Meta rate limits apply to our calls back to them, not to their webhook.
messenger.externalBlocker: A Meta app, page access from the business portfolio, and APP REVIEW for messaging permissions. Review takes weeks and can be refused.
messenger.externalActionRequired: Confirm WHO owns the page and the business portfolio, create the app, subscribe the page, pass App Review.
messenger.howWeTest: Simulate from DEV CONTROL with a Meta-shaped webhook body, signed with a test secret.
messenger.howWeGoLive: Deploy, set the callback URL and verify token at Meta, pass the handshake, send one real message, switch to live.
messenger.howWeDisable: Unsubscribe the page at Meta, or set the mode to off here.
messenger.operationalNote: Messenger shares the Meta Business Suite connection with Facebook and Instagram. It stays a separate channel for reporting, filtering, source and history, because a combined "Meta" number would hide where people actually came from.

instagram.label: Instagram
instagram.timestampSource: the event timestamp, milliseconds since epoch
instagram.externalBlocker: APP REVIEW for messaging permissions. The account is already Professional - it is in Meta Business Suite - so that part is settled and is not a blocker.
credentialsNeeded: a page or IG access token
instagram.externalActionRequired: Confirm the account is professional, link it to the app, request the permission, pass review.
instagram.operationalNote: Same shared Meta Business Suite inbox as Facebook.

whatsapp.label: WhatsApp
whatsapp.mechanism: WhatsApp Business Platform webhook, field messages.
whatsapp.timestampSource: the message timestamp, seconds since epoch
whatsapp.rateLimit: Messaging limits apply to what we SEND, not to what arrives.
whatsapp.externalBlocker: A phone number that is not already on consumer WhatsApp, and business verification.
whatsapp.externalActionRequired: Find a spare number, register it, verify the business.
whatsapp.howWeGoLive: Deploy, register the number, set the webhook, send one real message, switch to live.
whatsapp.howWeDisable: Remove the webhook at Meta, or set the mode to off here.
whatsapp.operationalNote: WhatsApp being part of the same Meta Business Suite inbox as Facebook and Instagram is NOT VERIFIED. Do not claim it. Access today: Ieva, Laura, Marina. Not Tetiana. Access is not ownership.

mailchimp.label: Mailchimp
mailchimp.mechanism: Audience webhook for subscribe, unsubscribe, profile and cleaned events.
mailchimp.externalIdSource: type + email + fired_at, because Mailchimp sends no event id
mailchimp.rateLimit: Not a concern for inbound events.
mailchimp.externalBlocker: EXTERNAL CONFIRMATION REQUIRED: whether the current Mailchimp plan includes webhooks.
credentialsNeeded: a secret we generate and put in the callback URL
mailchimp.externalActionRequired: Confirm the plan, then paste the URL into the audience webhook settings.
mailchimp.howWeGoLive: Deploy, paste the URL, trigger one subscribe, check it lands, switch to live.
mailchimp.identityNote: A Mailchimp event is ACTIVITY about somebody, not automatically a new person. It matches on the member id or the email. A newsletter subscriber is not a lead.

open_day.label: Open Day
open_day.mechanism: The existing booking tool posts a registration to our endpoint.
open_day.externalActionRequired: Point the existing booking tool at the endpoint.
open_day.howWeGoLive: Deploy, point the tool at it, make one real booking, switch to live.
open_day.identityNote: A registration attaches to an existing person when one matches, and never creates a second record for somebody we already hold. Attendance is a separate fact recorded later.
open_day._gap: Attendance is not yet linked back to the person record. The model is prepared; no attendance data is invented.

phone.label: Phone
phone.mechanism: We poll the TeleGroup PBX for recent calls.
phone.externalBlocker: An API token from TeleGroup, and the three deployment prerequisites.
credentialsNeeded: PBX_API_TOKEN, server side only, never in the client
phone.externalActionRequired: Ask TeleGroup for an API token for the calls endpoint.
phone.howWeTest: A local mock of the PBX list endpoint plus fixtures. The real API is never called in development.
phone.howWeGoLive: Deploy, set the token, apply sql/001, poll once by hand, check the rows, then enable the schedule.
phone._note: V1 logs calls by hand and says so on screen. The logger is built and tested locally and has never called the real API. The queue field gives us the button; that question is settled.
phone._answered: ANSWERED 24.09.2026, and it was in the brief all along. The event carries a `queue` field, and the queue IS the button: 1001*Q-ADMISSION is button 1, 1001*Q-COORDINATORS is button 2, 1001*Q-OTHER is button 3. config/prototype.json -> phoneMenu has mapped it since 23.09.2026. It was listed as an open question by mistake and Ritvars had to point that out.

agent.label: Agent or partner
agent.mechanism: A tokenised link the partner submits through, or a spreadsheet import.
providerControls: nothing standard - every agent is different
credentialsNeeded: one token per partner, issued by us
agent.externalActionRequired: Agree the format with each partner and issue their token.
agent.howWeGoLive: Issue a token to one partner, take one real referral, switch to live.
agent.identityNote: The agent is a SOURCE and an attribution. It is never automatically the CRM owner.
agent._note: No public agent API exists to integrate with. This is a contract we define, not one we discover.

in_person.label: In person
in_person.mechanism: A member of staff types it in at the desk.
in_person.howWeTest: Add a person from the app.
in_person.identityNote: Manual entry runs the SAME duplicate check as every automated channel. It is not a way around the rule.

linkedin.label: LinkedIn
linkedin.mechanism: UNKNOWN. No inbound message API is known to be available to us.
linkedin.externalIdSource: entered by the person copying it in
linkedin.timestampSource: entered by the person copying it in
linkedin.externalBlocker: EXTERNAL CONFIRMATION REQUIRED: whether LinkedIn offers any inbound messaging integration for a page like ours at all. Nothing has been confirmed. Do not promise it.
weControl: the normalised shape, so that IF a mechanism appears it maps in without redesign
linkedin.externalActionRequired: Somebody has to establish what, if anything, LinkedIn permits.
linkedin.howWeTest: Simulate from DEV CONTROL through the same normalised path.
linkedin.howWeGoLive: Not possible today. Manual entry only.
linkedin.operationalNote: Access today: Tetiana only. A LinkedIn contact often carries no email and no phone, so the handover gap to Admissions is real and the screen says so.

tiktok.label: TikTok
tiktok.mechanism: UNKNOWN. No inbound message API is known to be available to us.
tiktok.externalIdSource: entered by the person copying it in
tiktok.timestampSource: entered by the person copying it in
tiktok.externalBlocker: EXTERNAL CONFIRMATION REQUIRED: whether TikTok offers any inbound messaging integration. Nothing has been confirmed. Do not invent one.
tiktok.externalActionRequired: Somebody has to establish what, if anything, TikTok permits.
tiktok.howWeTest: Simulate from DEV CONTROL through the same normalised path.
tiktok.howWeGoLive: Not possible today. Manual entry only.
tiktok.operationalNote: Access today: Tetiana only. Same handover gap as LinkedIn.

_meta: Facebook, Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp are reached through ONE Meta Business Suite connection. That is an integration detail. Each remains a SEPARATE channel in the CRM for reporting, filtering, source and history: there is deliberately no combined "Meta" number, because it would hide where people actually came from. WhatsApp being inside the same shared inbox is NOT VERIFIED and must not be claimed.
